title: SLO telemetry consolidation and Grade-of-Service dashboard
creator: Liam O'Connor
description:
Goal: consolidate disparate golden-signal streams and token-level SLI derivations into a single Grade-of-Service (GoS) dashboard that product owners and SREs can use to understand SLO burn, regional failover state, and active load-shedding behavior. This ticket covers the telemetry plumbing, provenance tagging for token-SLIs, dashboard design and the first canary rollout for one region. We will not change enforcement behavior in this ticket; only visibility and alerting tiers are in scope.

Motivation: multiple dashboards exist with overlapping metrics (latency p95/p99, admit rates, kv cache hit, circuit state) but inconsistent labels and different rollup windows. This causes noisy alerts and long troubleshooting time during cross-region incidents. Consolidation will reduce mean time to detect and triage, enable SLO-driven runbooks, and make regional failover decisions auditable.
acceptance_criteria: All golden signals (request rate, error rate, latency) are exposed with unified tag set: region, shard, route, admission_result, model_variant, kv_cache_hit
Token-level SLI derivation pipeline emits provenance headers to allow backtrace from SLI to request and shard for p95/p99 windows
GoS dashboard contains panels for per-region SLO burn, admission queue depth, active circuit breakers with state history, and KV cache hitmap
Alerts created for SLO burn > 2x target for 5 minutes, and for sudden increase in admission rejections in any region
Canary deployment in eu-west-1 for one production route with no user-impacting regressions for 72h
implementation_notes: Plan: 1) Add a telemetry enrichment step in the front-door proxy that attaches canonical labels (region, route, shard, admission_result, token_bucket_id) to traces and metrics. 2) Extend tokenized SLI aggregator to include provenance ids so that an alert on SLI can produce a minimal trace of example request ids and admission states. 3) Implement multi-resolution rollups (1m/5m/1h) for p95/p99 to reduce ingestion cost. 4) Build Grafana dashboard using templated variables for region/route/model_variant. Tech trade-offs: we will sample full traces at 1:100 to avoid trace ingestion blowup; provenance metadata is small (<= 128 bytes) and added to existing metric tags. If storage becomes a bottleneck we'll switch rollups to histogram buckets exported at the exporter layer.
rollout_plan: Phase 1 (Week 1): instrumentation in staging, dashboard preview, smoke tests. Phase 2 (Week 2): canary in eu-west-1 for route /v1/generate with 5% traffic diversion, monitor SLI and alert noise. Phase 3 (Week 3): expand to us-west-2 and ap-southeast-1 if canary passes 72h. Phase 4: update runbooks and promote alerts to paging after one successful week of stable metrics. Rollback criteria: any user-visible p99 regression > 20% or >5 customer reports in 1h triggers immediate rollback of telemetry flag and investigation.
dashboard_panels: GoS - aggregated SLO burn by region (heatmap)
Admission pipeline - queue depth and processing latency (timeseries)
Circuit Manager - active circuits with open/closed/half-open timeline per shard
Token-SLI - p95/p99 by token-length buckets with provenance link
KV cache - hit ratio heatmap by route and model_variant
Fallback ratio - percentage of requests routed to fallback models
Sampled traces - example trace links for top SLI offenders (1:100 sampling)
